public_rationale: His firm prediction is that OpenAI and Anthropic will both start charging customers more. He gave no deadline. He hedged the token-billing and subscription-cut parts as 'very likely', so the contract does not require them. Both companies were moving toward an IPO: Anthropic filed an S-1 on 2026-10-26, and OpenAI's IPO was expected in early 2027 (e2). On 2026-06-15, a secondary summary reported that Anthropic had paused a planned billing change for Agent SDK usage and that subscription limits were unchanged (e1). That is not a price rise. No evidence item shows either company raising the list price or per-token rate of an existing product between 2026-06-08 and 2026-10-28. With no deadline, the lack of a rise so far does not make the forecast wrong. The early-support rule has not been met, so the forecast stays open.
limitations: Several pricing sources could not be read (HTTP 403, 410 and 429 errors), including an OpenAI page on Codex pricing for teams. A price rise could have been missed.
One secondary source said ChatGPT Plus rose to $24 from June 15, 2026. It could not be read or checked, and other sources list $20.
The contract does not count tighter usage limits at the same price as a price rise. The evidence does not show whether such changes happened, and some readers could call them charging more.
e1 is a secondary summary, not Anthropic's own notice.

statement.excerpt: To make matters worse, both OpenAI and Anthropic are speeding as fast as they can toward IPO — which means that both will have to start looking like real companies, which means both will, inevitably, start charging their customers more and very likely moving the vast majority of them to token-based billing and either kill or vastly limit their subsidized subscriptions.

our_interpretation: The firm commitment is only that both companies will start charging customers more. The billing shift and the subscription cuts are marked 'very likely', so they are hedged. They are described in the commentary but are not required for support.
The IPO race is the stated reason, not a condition. Support does not require proof that the IPO caused any price rise.

Plain reading of 'charging more': each company raises the price customers pay for an existing paid product after the post. That means a higher list price for an existing subscription tier, or a higher per-token rate for the same model. A new, more expensive tier is not a rise for existing customers. Cutting usage limits at the same price is an arguable effective rise, but it is not counted on its…
criteria.support_condition: After 2026-06-08, both OpenAI and Anthropic each raise the price customers pay for an existing paid product, such as a subscription list price or a per-token rate for the same model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, no single event contradicts the forecast. It could only be judged false if one or both companies plainly never raised prices over a long period after reaching IPO. No such period has passed.
